ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Figure A is a schematic diagram of a small AC generator. The coil rotates counterclockwise, and the generated electromotive force (EMF) varies sinusoidally with time, as shown in Figure B. The generator coil has 300 turns and an internal resistance of 1Ω, while the external bulb has a constant resistance of 9Ω.

1. How much electrical energy does the generator output in 1 second?
2. At the moment of $1\times{10}^{-2}\mathrm{s}$, what is the magnetic flux through the coil?

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Figure A is a schematic diagram of a small AC generator. The coil rotates counterclockwise, and the generated electromotive force (EMF) varies sinusoidally with time, as shown in Figure B. The generator coil has 300 turns and an internal resistance of 1Ω, while the external bulb has a constant resistance of 9Ω. 1. How much electrical energy does the generator output in 1 second? 2. At the moment of $1\times{10}^{-2}\mathrm{s}$, what is the magnetic flux through the coil?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description first: Figure A shows a small AC generator coil rotating between magnetic poles and connected to an external circuit containing a bulb. Figure B is an EMF-time sinusoidal graph: the vertical axis is e/V, the horizontal axis is t/(×10^-2 s), the peak EMF is +6√2 V, the trough is -6√2 V, and one full period is from 0 to 2×10^-2 s. Reasoning: From the graph, the peak EMF is E_m=6√2 V, so the RMS EMF is E_rms=E_m/√2=6 V. The coil has internal resistance r=1 Ω and the bulb resistance is R=9 Ω, so the total resistance is R_total=10 Ω. Thus the RMS current is I_rms=E_rms/R_total=6/10=0.6 A. The electrical energy delivered to the bulb in 1 s is W=I_rms^2 R t=(0.6)^2×9×1=3.24 J. For the magnetic flux, the period is T=2×10^-2 s, so the angular speed is ω=2π/T=100π rad/s. For sinusoidal rotation, the peak induced EMF satisfies E_m=NωΦ_m. With N=300, Φ_m=E_m/(Nω)=6√2/(300×100π)=√2/(5000π) Wb. At t=1×10^-2 s, the graph shows the EMF is zero, corresponding to an extremal magnetic flux, so the flux magnitude is √2/(5000π) Wb.
